title: feat(entity): add a command to declare standards on an entity
description: No strspc command writes the standards field on an entity, so declaring a standard (e.g. on KWRD) needs a hand edit plus 'strspc entity rehash'. Add 'strspc entity standards add <EUID> --id --relation [--version]' that validates (STDREF-002/004/007), rejects duplicates and rehashes. GH issue: https://github.com/SteerSpec/strspc-CLI/issues/204
design:
PLAN (explored; manager v1.36.0 already provides the validation, so the CLI is thin)

Command: strspc entity standards add <EUID> --id <slug> --relation implements|derived_from [--version V] [--url U] [--dir ./rules] [--json]
Command: strspc entity standards remove <EUID> --id <slug> [--dir] [--json]   (optional; ship add first, remove in the same PR only if cheap)

Reuse (no new engine code):
- entity.ValidateStandardRef(ref)  -> STDREF-002/004/008 id, relation, url checks
- entity.FindStandard(refs, id)    -> duplicate detection (STDREF-003)
- resolveEntityTarget + modifyEntity (src/cmd/rule_helpers.go) -> locates top-level or sub-entity, bumps ancestor patch versions (RD007), refreshes hashes via entityops.UpdateMeta. Same pattern as note_add.go.

Files:
1. src/cmd/entity_standards.go       newEntityStandardsCmd() group + newEntityStandardsAddCmd() (+ remove)
2. src/cmd/entity.go                 cmd.AddCommand(newEntityStandardsCmd())
3. src/cmd/entity_standards_test.go  table tests, modelled on note_add_test.go / entity_add_test.go
4. README.md                         add row to command table + short example in the "Report coverage of a standard" section

Behaviour decisions:
- --id and --relation required. --version optional: when empty OMIT it (schema rejects an empty string, STDREF-007); only set the field when non-empty after TrimSpace.
- Duplicate id on the same entity -> error (STDREF-003). No silent update; an 'update' is out of scope.
- Inside mutate: append ref, then entityops.UpdateMeta(f) so version/hash are refreshed like note add does. Test that the target rule_set.version rises.
- JSON output: entity_id, file, standard (the ref), version old->new.
- Realm-level standards (realm.json) are OUT OF SCOPE; file a follow-up bead if wanted.

Tests (TDD, write first):
- add to top-level entity: field written, hash valid (rehashEntity reports no change), version bumped
- add to sub-entity: ancestors' versions bumped
- bad id slug, bad relation, bad url -> error, file untouched
- duplicate id -> error, file untouched
- empty version omitted from JSON; --version written when given
- unknown EUID -> error; --json shape
- end to end: after add, 'strspc standards coverage' lists the standard as declared

Verify: make fmt && make lint && make test. Then dogfood on rules/core/KWRD.json only if the other session has not already hand-edited it (coordinate; do not collide).

title: realm validate --recursive --strict passes overrides that strspc check rejects (RR015, RR023, RR024)
description:
On strspc 1.41.1, strspc realm validate <realm> --recursive --strict and strspc lint print 'No errors or warnings found' for a realm whose overrides break the chain and visibility rules. strspc check --static-only on the same realm reports 5 errors and 1 warning: RR015 (override of a rule an ancestor already replaced), RR023 x3 (override of a protected Entity's rule from another realm), RR024 (child Entity wider than the Entity it inherits) and RR016 as a warning (override of a Retired rule). strspc render prints RR015, RR023 and RR024 too, but only as warnings on stderr, and it exits 0.

Repro: a realm with a local-path dependency on a second realm; an Entity that inherits a dependency Entity marked visibility protected; a rule that overrides one of its rules; a grandchild Entity that overrides a rule its parent already overrides. Run the three commands above.

Found in the strspc-rules assessment of 2026-11-25 (strspc-rules-9sf). Related: strspc-manager-4oy, filed earlier for the same gap before strspc check was compared.

Tree, as realmlint/linked.go judges it when validating --dir: the realm at --dir, its parent (entity.ParentRealm) when --dir is a sub-realm, and its direct sub_realms; a declaration anywhere in it counts. Whether X's manifest is kind standard needs a fetch and is left to realm validate.
1. checkStandardRealmDeclared(dir, ref) in standards_core.go: refuses when ref.Realm is declared by no realm of the tree, hint: realm dep add X@<version> --dir <dir>. No realm.json at --dir: skipped (as checkCoreAccepts).
2. Called by realm standards add and entity standards add (after checkCoreAcceptsStandardLink), and by realm/entity standards update when --realm is given; --clear-realm needs none.
3. realm dep remove X refuses while a Standard Reference of the tree (manifests and entities, rulelint.WalkRealmStandards) links to X and no other realm of the tree declares X; lists the references to clear or remove first.
4. Help: standardRealmUsage and the add Long text say the dependency is checked on write.
5. Tests: undeclared refused with hint; declared by self, by a sub-realm, by the parent from a sub-realm; no realm.json skipped; update --realm refused, --clear-realm fine; dep remove refused while linked, allowed once cleared or when another realm of the tree declares it.
6. Docs: docs/author-rules.md where linked Standard References are described.
Edge: a dep declared only by a sibling sub-realm passes when validating the parent but not the sub-realm alone; the check mirrors validate on the same --dir.

title: Limit which repo owners receive the GitHub token
description: realm validate, realm dep upgrade and check send GITHUB_TOKEN when fetching any github:// source, including those named in a cloned realm.json. The token goes only to api.github.com, not to a third party, but a crafted realm can make strspc read a private repo the token can reach and surface its content in diagnostics. A CLI-only fix can't cover it: remote.Fetcher holds one Token for all refs, and check shares it with ruleresolve and realmresolve, so strspc-manager needs a per-owner hook first, then a release, then the CLI wiring. Defaulting to SteerSpec alone would break private dependencies under other owners, such as a consumer's own org. Proposed default: SteerSpec plus GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER, extended by a STRSPC_TOKEN_OWNERS env var, with a 404 error that names that variable.

Decide whether to refuse a link in saveEntity (or modifyEntity) for every writer, using isLinkPath, as entity rehash <EUID> now does.

title: entity rehash --all writes through symlinked entity files
description: Found while fixing Copilot's finding on #238 (31a3b29, rewrite-added-by). entity rehash --all walks with entity.WalkEntityFiles, which reads through a symlinked .json, and saves with saveEntity (os.WriteFile), which writes through it, so a link under --dir can make rehash rewrite a file outside it. Apply the same rule as rewrite-added-by: Lstat each path, list links and never follow them.
design:
Scope (chosen 2026-11-05): --all and the single-EUID form; other writers go to a follow-up bead.
- Shared helper isLinkPath(path) (bool, error) via os.Lstat in rule_helpers.go; realm rewrite-added-by switches to it (no behaviour change).
- --all: Lstat before parseErr; a link (dangling too) goes to rehashResult.Links (json "links", [] never null), is never read or written. Human: "Skipped <path> (a symbolic link, not followed: rehash its target where it lives)". Summary counts links in skipped. A link to a file inside --dir is still skipped; the target is rehashed once on its own.
- rehash <EUID>: when the resolved path is a link, fail before reading: "<path> is a symbolic link; rehash its target where it lives". Nothing written.
- Help text of entity rehash mentions links.
- Tests: link to a stale file outside --dir (outside unchanged, link listed, real files still rehashed, JSON links = [link]); dangling link listed, no error; link inside --dir to a stale sibling (sibling rehashed once, link listed); single EUID on a link errors, target unchanged; skip when os.Symlink fails (Windows CI). Mutation: drop the Lstat check -> tests fail.
- Follow-up bead: saveEntity / modifyEntity writers (rule add, note add/update, rule supersede, entity standards, ...) write through a linked entity file.
acceptance_criteria: A test with a link to a file outside --dir: the outside file is unchanged and the link is reported.
notes: PR #248 (fix/rehash-links). Close this bead when #248 merges. Follow-up for other writers: strspc-cli-5gl.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #248 (merged 2026-11-05). Other writers: strspc-cli-5gl.

title: feat: add `strspc doctor` diagnostic command
description:
## Why

Users have no way to diagnose environment issues with their strspc installation.
A `doctor` command (similar to `brew doctor`, `gh doctor`, etc.) would surface
common problems automatically.

## What needs to be done

Implement `strspc doctor` as a new top-level command that checks:

- Binary is on PATH and symlinks resolve correctly
- Installed version vs latest available (update check)
- Realm directory structure validity (reuse `realm validate` logic)
- Any required config files are present and well-formed
- Optional: OS/arch compatibility, Go runtime info

Output should be human-readable with pass/warn/fail indicators per check.
Support `--json` flag for structured output (consistent with other commands).

## Acceptance criteria

- `strspc doctor` runs a suite of checks and exits 0 if all pass, non-zero if any fail
- Each check emits a labelled status line (✓ / ⚠ / ✗)
- `--json` flag emits structured results
- Command registered in root.go following existing Cobra patterns
design:
# Design: `strspc doctor`

## Purpose and how it differs from `status`
`strspc status` reports how things stand: config, sources, rule counts, realm.
`strspc doctor` judges them. Every check gets pass / warn / fail, and each warn or
fail comes with a one-line remedy, a command the user can run. Doctor reuses
`collectStatus` for the source states instead of duplicating it.

Doctor never fails because the project is broken. A config that doesn't parse is
a failed check, not a command error. Doctor itself errors only on bad flags.

## Usage
```
strspc doctor [path] [--online] [--strict] [--json]
```
- `path` is the project root, `.` by default, the same as `status`.
- Offline by default, like `status`: no network calls, no writes, no cache fills.
- `--online` adds the checks that need the network (§Online).
- `--strict` turns warns into fails, the same as `lint --strict`.

## Exit codes (src/cmd/exit.go)
- 0: no check failed.
- 1 (`exitViolations`): at least one check failed, or a warn under `--strict`.
- 2 (`exitConfig`): bad flags or an unreadable `path`.

Doctor doesn't use exit 3 (`exitUnavailable`). A missing API key is a warn.

## Checks
Each check has a stable ID (`group.name`) that appears in the JSON output and can be
used in docs. Remedies are shown in parentheses.

### install
- `install.version`: the binary version. A `dev` or empty version (not a release
  build) is a warn (`install a release: see README`).
- `install.path`: `exec.LookPath("strspc")` resolves to the running binary, compared
  with symlinks evaluated (`filepath.EvalSymlinks`).
  - Not on PATH: warn.
  - A different binary earlier on PATH shadows this one: warn, naming both paths.
- `install.platform`: GOOS/GOARCH and the Go runtime version. Info only, always pass.

### tools
- `tools.git`: `git` is on PATH. `diff`, `refs` and `check --diff` need it.
  Missing is a warn, or a fail when the project is inside a git repository.

### config
- `config.present`: a missing config is a warn (`strspc init`), and the remaining
  config and source checks are skipped, not failed.
- `config.parse`: the YAML decodes (`parseStrspcConfig`).
- `config.schema`: the config validates against the cached config schema
  (`validateConfigSchema`, cache only). If the schema isn't cached, the check is
  skipped (`strspc sync`, or run with `--online`).
- `config.ttl`: `cache.ttl` parses with `time.ParseDuration`.
- `config.states`: `fail_on` and `evaluate_on` hold only known state codes.
- `config.provider`: `evaluator.provider` is a known provider, `claude` or `null`
  (the same switch as `buildProvider`, without building a client).

### credentials
- `credentials.provider`: when the provider is `claude`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set.
  Unset is a warn, not a fail: `check` would exit 3 until a key is set, but
  a project can still be linted and validated without one
  (`export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or set evaluator.provider: null`). With
  `--strict` it fails, like every warn.
  - The key's value is never printed. The check reports only set or unset.
- `credentials.github`: for each `github://` source, whether a token
  (`remote.TokenFromEnv`) would be sent to that owner (`remote.TokenForOwner`).
  - No token, or an owner the token isn't allowed for, is a warn: public repos
    still work, private ones fail. The remedy names `GITHUB_TOKEN` or
    `STRSPC_TOKEN_OWNERS`.

### sources (one result per configured source, from `collectStatus`)
- `local`, `pinned`, `fresh`: pass.
- `stale`, `not_synced`: warn (`strspc sync`).
- `missing`, `invalid`, `unsupported`: fail, with the error that `status` shows.

### realm (for each local source that has a `realm.json`)
- `realm.validate`: runs the same lint as `realm validate`, and reports only the
  error and warning counts (`strspc realm validate <dir>` for details).
- `realm.core`: when the realm declares standards, the core pin accepts them
  (`corePinFor` and `checkCoreAcceptsStandards`). Otherwise a fail, with the
  `corePinRemedy` hint.
- No separate schema-drift check. RM015 (the `_schema/` files match the core pin)
  is already part of `realm validate`. It runs offline when the core dependency
  is cached; otherwise `--online` lets it fetch the dependency.

### project
- `project.gitignore`: `.strspc/cache/` and `.strspc/cache.db` are git-ignored
  (`git check-ignore`). A tracked cache is a warn.
- `project.ci`: a workflow that runs `strspc check` exists under `.github/workflows/`.
  If none exists, the result is info only (`strspc ci init`).

### Online (`--online` only)
- `online.latest`: compares the running version with
  `GET /repos/SteerSpec/strspc-CLI/releases/latest`. An older version is a warn.
  Dev builds skip this check.
- `online.sources`: each `github://` source resolves (a HEAD request or a ref
  lookup via the manager `remote` package), with the token sent to allowed owners
  only. Unreachable is a fail; rate-limited is a warn.
- `online.provider`: no API call is made, because it would cost money. Key
  presence (checked above) is enough.

## Output
Human output uses the existing styles (`brandStyle`, `descStyle`):
```
strspc doctor
install
  ✓ version        v1.42.0
  ⚠ path           /usr/local/bin/strspc shadows ~/go/bin/strspc
config
  ✓ parse
credentials
  ⚠ provider       ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set
                   → export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or set evaluator.provider: null
sources
  ✗ ./rules        missing: directory does not exist
...
1 failed, 2 warnings, 14 passed
```
Text from the repo or the config goes through `printableDiagnostic` / `sanitizeLine`
before it is printed.

JSON output:
```json
{"version":"…","checks":[{"id":"credentials.provider","group":"credentials",
  "status":"warn","message":"…","remedy":"…"}],
 "summary":{"pass":14,"warn":2,"fail":1,"skip":0}}
```
`checks` is always an array, never null. The status values are pass, warn, fail,
skip and info.

## Code structure
- `src/cmd/doctor.go`: the command, the runner and the output.
- `src/cmd/doctor_checks.go`: one function per group, each
  `func(*doctorEnv) []doctorResult`.
- `doctorEnv` injects everything that touches the host: `getenv`, `lookPath`,
  `executable`, `httpClient`, `cwd` and `now`. Tests don't depend on the real PATH,
  environment or network, and `--online` tests use `httptest`.
- No manager change is needed. Everything above uses existing manager APIs
  (`remote`, `realmlint`, `rulelint`, `schema`) or CLI helpers. The release check
  stays in the CLI, because it concerns the CLI binary.

## Out of scope
- `--fix`: doctor reports and suggests, and never modifies files. A fix mode could
  follow later, behind its own flag.
- Validating the API key with a provider call.

## Delivery
1. PR 1: the offline checks (install, tools, config, credentials, sources, realm,
   project), JSON output, `--strict`, and a README entry.
2. PR 2: `--online` (latest release, source reachability).

A rule for the command's contract (exit codes, read-only by default) can be added
as Draft in PR 1 via `strspc rule add`, and promoted once the command ships.

## Decisions (2026-11-02)
1. Warns exit 0; `--strict` makes them fail.
2. `realm.validate` runs by default. Run time is not a concern, so there is no
   `--deep` flag.
3. A missing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with provider `claude` is a warn.
notes: PR 1 merged: https://github.com/SteerSpec/strspc-CLI/pull/219 (offline checks, --json, --strict, README, Draft CMD-006/CMD-007). PR 2 merged: https://github.com/SteerSpec/strspc-CLI/pull/224 (--online: online.latest, online.sources). Deviation from design: --online adds only the two GitHub reads; schema and dependency lookups stay cache-only, so doctor never writes. Remaining: promote CMD-006/007 D->P (now) and P->I, each in its own PR.

title: note update on a Note new in the branch bumps its revision, so diff fails RD015
description: Reported from strspc-rules PR #198 (strspc 1.41.1). A Note added in a branch with 'strspc note add' (revision 0) and then reworded with 'strspc note update' goes to revision 1; 'strspc diff --base origin/develop' then fails RD015 ('new note must have revision 0'). A Note can't be removed (NTE-009) and no command lowers a revision, so the only ways out are a hand edit plus rehash, or rebuilding the file from the base. A review round that asks to reword a new Note hits this every time.
design: Implemented: --base <ref> on note update and rule update, no default (diff's default base is HEAD, where a committed note already exists, so no default would help). With --base, the revision is set against the entity file at ref: 0 when absent, base+1 when changed, base revision when it reads as at the base (RD004, RD013, RD015). Without --base, behaviour is unchanged. NTE-008 wording ('0 when the Note is added') should be clarified in strspc-rules: added = present on the base branch (PLB chose this reading 2026-11-26).
acceptance_criteria: note update on a Note absent at the base leaves revision 0 and refreshes hashes; diff passes; a Note present at the base still bumps; tests for both.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #345 (note update / rule update --base)

title: refs: report rules that no file cites (coverage check) (GH #261)
description: GH #261: refs checks that cited rules exist and are live, but not the reverse. Hand-maintained rule ID lists in prompts and docs go stale when a rule is added (strspc-marketing PR #22). Add a coverage check reporting rules no file cites.
